nodes.title: Adapt to upstream heap profiling changes
nodes.body:
Heads-up to WG Upgrades:

Chromium is changing how heap profiling works upstream: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8258807

They’re adding it as a Perfetto data source and deleting the memlog infrastructure that Electron has been using for heap profiling so far.

When upgrading Chromium, this will probably require breaking API changes on Electron’s side:

1. Thoughts on the preferred API shape:
    - Drop the dedicated `contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()`
    - Probably just roll it into `contentTracing.startRecording()` as described in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51184
2. How to find the code to delete:
    - Start with https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50826
    - Delete any code added back then that is no longer necessary
3. Reference for how the integration can work:
    - Chromium's own usage of the API: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8263276
    - The CL that added the Perfetto data source: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8163651
    - [Comment](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8258807/comments/9f802612_c2ae7079) by the upstream Chromium author: "it boils down to adding `ChromiumSamplingHeapProfilerConfig` to the perfetto proto config"

nodes.title: Support non-activating, keyboard-focusable panels for immersive, Spotlight-like AI chat input
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Electron does not provide a supported macOS window mode for an immersive, Spotlight-like AI chat input panel that can receive keyboard input without activating the Electron application or becoming the main window.

The desired interaction is an immersive AI chat input surface: the panel appears above the user's current application, accepts a question immediately, and leaves the current application visually and semantically active. The currently exposed concepts do not express this combination. win.showInactive() can show a window without focusing it, but it does not provide a path for the window to later receive keyboard input while remaining non-activating. Conversely, a regular focused window takes application focus, while win.setFocusable(false) prevents the window from becoming a key window and therefore prevents keyboard interaction.

This leaves applications without a reliable way to create an input-capable, non-activating surface on macOS.



### Proposed Solution

Proposed API

One possible macOS-only API is an activable panel option and matching runtime setter:

Plain Text


const panel = new BrowserWindow({
  type: 'panel',
  activable: false,
});

panel.setActivable(false);



With activable: false, the panel would remain eligible to become a key window when focusable is true, but it would not become the main window. This keeps main-window activation separate from keyboard focus.

See PR https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/52914



### Alternatives Considered

No.

### Additional Information

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7071a103-d865-4d01-adf7-07d5f19ed00e

nodes.body:

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.8.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.5854

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

After capturing an individual application window, resizing the captured window should not terminate the Electron application. Capture should continue using the new window dimensions.


### Actual Behavior

Window capture starts successfully and frames are produced normally.

When the user continuously resizes the captured application window, total CPU usage rises to approximately 100%. After several seconds, the entire Electron browser process terminates without a JavaScript exception.

The problem is reproducible on the affected Windows 10 computer, but not on most newer computers.


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/307914070/14a2fd13dd155037f8a36ceb39819149

### Additional Information

### Reproduction steps

1. Open an external application such as Notepad.
2. Start capturing that individual application window.
3. Continuously drag an edge of the captured window to change its width and height.
4. Total CPU usage reaches approximately 100%, followed by a native crash after several seconds.

This uses direct individual-window capture through `desktopCapturer` / `chromeMediaSource`. It is not full-screen capture followed by region cropping.

### Affected machine

- Intel Core i5-3470
- 8 GB RAM
- 1920 × 1080 display
- Microsoft Basic Display Adapter, driver 10.0.19041.3636
- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.5854

The failure mainly appears on a small number of older Windows 10 integrated-graphics systems. Reducing capture resolution, frame rate, and encoder bitrate did not prevent the crash.

### Related issues

- #47450 reports a crash while refreshing the `desktopCapturer.getSources()` list; this report crashes during an active window-capture session while resizing the source window.
- #51910 concerns WGC thumbnail capture errors in a different Electron version; this report concerns active individual-window capture.

<details>
<summary>Native crash evidence</summary>

A minidump from an affected run showed native C++ exception code `0xE06D7363`. Loaded graphics modules included `GraphicsCapture.dll`, `d3d11.dll`, `dxgi.dll`, and `d3d10warp.dll`.

WGC responds to source-window size changes by recreating capture-frame-pool and texture resources. The presence of `d3d10warp.dll` together with Microsoft Basic Display Adapter suggests that this machine may be entering a software-rendering path when those resources are repeatedly recreated.

</details>

nodes.title: Opaque frameless windows jitter during native interactive resize with default ANGLE/OpenGL on Linux/X11
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.4.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, GNOME Shell 42.9, X11, Linux 6.16.7, Mesa 23.2.1

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not yet established for Electron's default ANGLE/OpenGL backend. The same Electron 43.4.1 build resizes smoothly when explicitly configured to use ANGLE/Vulkan.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Not directly testable using the equivalent Electron `BrowserWindow` configuration.

### Expected Behavior

An opaque frameless X11 window should resize with stable visual presentation when using Electron's default graphics configuration. Its content and apparent window edges should follow the native interactive resize without jumping or lagging.

### Actual Behavior

Quickly resizing an opaque `BrowserWindow` with `frame: false` vertically or diagonally produces visible presentation jitter when Electron is launched without a `--use-angle` override.

A matched comparison using the same Electron 43.4.1 build, the same `BrowserWindow` options, and the same native edge/corner resize interaction is smooth when Vulkan is selected explicitly:

| Graphics configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `--use-angle` not set — default ANGLE/OpenGL | Visible resize jitter |
| `--use-angle=vulkan` with `Vulkan,DefaultANGLEVulkan,VulkanFromANGLE` enabled | Smooth |

No JavaScript resizing, IPC bounds updates, `setBounds()`, or custom resize implementation is involved.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/otanim/12c2cece789b68d04c271b96bfc41b68

### Additional Information

Confirmed on Intel Meteor Lake-P / Intel Arc Graphics using the i915 driver.

#### Correction to the original investigation

The earlier Alpha 3 versus Alpha 4 comparison and source-commit attribution were confounded by a separate Electron regression that prevented transparent frameless windows from being resized natively on Linux.

That separate native-resizing regression affected the Electron versions used during the earlier investigation. It was fixed for Electron 43.x in 43.4.1 by #52947, a backport of #52740. The corresponding 44.x backport is #52891.

Because native resizing was unavailable during part of the earlier comparison, alternative resize paths did not provide an equivalent test of Electron's native interactive resize behavior and produced false-positive conclusions. The previous claim that the jitter itself began in `43.0.0-alpha.4`, along with the associated first-bad source-commit attribution and proposed opaque-surface policy, is therefore withdrawn.

After retesting with native resize restored in Electron 43.4.1, the reproducible differentiator is the graphics backend: the default ANGLE/OpenGL path jitters, while the explicitly selected ANGLE/Vulkan path is smooth.

The proposed implementation restores the pre-43 opaque surface policy for opaque frameless X11 windows, disables alpha-dependent client-frame shadow insets on that path, and relies on PR #52740's internal resize band. Genuine transparent windows and Wayland CSD windows remain translucent.

nodes.title: Flaky test: nn-test — short tls/https Node tests die with a silent SIGABRT (exitcode -6)
nodes.body:
Random tests in the Node.js suite (`linux-x64 / nn-test / Run Node.js Tests`) die with a silent SIGABRT — no stderr, no stack — and pass 9/9 on the `--measure-flakiness` rerun, which still fails the job. The victim is a different test each time but always one that loads `tls`/`https` and exits quickly.

**Test:** any short `parallel/test-tls-*` / `parallel/test-https-*` (seen: `test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra`, `test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra-empty`, `test-https-argument-of-creating`)
**Job:** `linux-x64 / nn-test / Run Node.js Tests` (`script/node-spec-runner.js`)
**Platform:** linux x64 (the bug is cross-platform, this is just where we run the suite)
**Frequency:** 3 of the last 34 completed nn-test jobs (2026-08-14 → 08-16), all on unrelated PR branches, each `failed 1 out of 10` on rerun. Locally ~1 in 30k test processes at `-j128`; `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 electron -e "require('tls')"` hits it ~1 in 700.
**Error / signal:** `severity: crashed` / `exitcode: -6`, or from `test/common/child_process.js`: `status = null, signal = SIGABRT` with empty `--- stderr ---` / `--- stdout ---`.

**Failing runs:**
- https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/31939048118/job/95146708674 (`test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra`)
- https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/31934729186/job/95136834082 (`test-https-argument-of-creating`)
- https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/31909127762/job/95072968384 (`test-tls-get-ca-certificates-extra-empty`)

**Cause:** since Node 24.9 (nodejs/node#59856) `require('tls')` starts a `uv_thread` that loads the CA certificates and then takes `per_process::cli_options_mutex`. Node joins it in `node::TearDownOncePerProcess()`, which we never call, so if the process exits first the static mutex is destroyed by `exit()` under the thread and libuv's `uv_mutex_lock` `abort()`s. Core from a local repro:

```
main thread:                          crashing thread:
  exit() → _dl_fini (static dtors)      abort()
  __libc_start_main                     uv_mutex_lock()               deps/uv/src/unix/thread.c:366
                                        node::crypto::LoadCACertificates()  src/crypto/crypto_context.cc:934
```

Not limited to `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`: `require('node:tls'); app.exit()` before `ready` in the browser process aborts ~1 in 5. All of 41–44-x-y ship Node 24.18 and are affected.

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

### Expected Behavior

On subscribing to a protected characteristic, the pairing handler should trigger in the electron main process (which has been set using `ses.setBluetoothPairingHandler((details, callback) => { ... })`), allowing to confirm the pairing and read/write/subscribe to the protected characteristic.

### Actual Behavior

**First**: Initial pairing works fine.
After connecting, once I try to subscribe to a characteristic that is protected, the electron pairing handler is called in the main process and allows me to confirm the pairing.

But this behaviour differs, once the central (windows) forgets the bond information (e.g. user deleted it through windows settings) and the peripheral still has the bond information stored.

In this asymmetric state subscribing to the characteristic fails with `GATT Error: Not paired.` It does not trigger the pairing handler, which it should.

Interestingly this does not happen, when I try to connect using Windows System Settings. Here connecting works fine, a new pairing is automatically initiated. It also does not happend on my Android phone (not via Web BLE). So this must be some specific error of the chromium/electron stack.

_No response_

_No response_

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.1.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.6 (25G70) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — I have not found a version that does not abort in this environment. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Launching Electron on a Mac that cannot register with Launch Services should print an error and exit with a non-zero status. The process should not `abort()`. ### Actual Behavior The process dies immediately (~100–200 ms) with `SIGABRT` / `abort()` before any app JavaScript runs. macOS writes a crash report: ``` abort ___RegisterApplication_block_invoke _RegisterApplication GetCurrentProcess -[NSApplication init] +[NSApplication sharedApplication] ElectronMain ``` Exit code is 134. nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

34.5.8

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10.0.22631 (build 6060/26100-series)

### What arch are you using?

ia32

### Last Known Working Electron version

22.3.26

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The GPU process does not crash frequently.

### Actual Behavior

After upgrading our Electron app from 22.3.6 to 34.5.8, we started seeing frequent GPU process crashes, even with --disable-gpu set. The crash occurs in Skia's SIMD raster pipeline (hsw::lowp::gather_8888, using the AVX2 vpgatherdd instruction), triggered through Chromium's software compositing fallback path (viz::SoftwareRenderer), not the hardware GPU path. Since --disable-gpu forces Chromium into this CPU/Skia compositing path, the flag does not avoid the crash — it routes all rendering into the exact code path that's crashing.

Crash details
Exception: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ (0xC0000005), read from 0x46cc913c
Faulting function: hsw::lowp::gather_8888 / hsw::lowp::gather (vpgatherdd ymm4, dword ptr [eax+ymm1*4], ymm3)
OS: Windows 10.0.22631 (build 6060/26100-series)
CPU: Intel family 6, model 186 (0xBA) — 13th Gen "Raptor Lake" (mobile, e.g. i7-1360P class), 16 logical CPUs, fully AVX2-capable, not a legacy/edge-case CPU
GPU: unknown (crash happens in the software renderer, independent of GPU vendor/driver)

Call stack (top frames)
hsw::lowp::gather (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:5883)
hsw::lowp::gather_8888_k (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:6032)
hsw::lowp::gather_8888 (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:6029)
hsw::lowp::seed_shader (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:5580)
hsw::lowp::start_pipeline (SkRasterPipeline_opts.h:5160)
SkRasterPipelineBlitter::blitRectWithTrace (SkRasterPipelineBlitter.cpp:431)
SkRasterPipelineBlitter::blitRect (SkRasterPipelineBlitter.cpp:394)
SkScan::FillIRect (SkScan.cpp:45)
SkScan::FillRect (SkScan.cpp:108)
SkDrawBase::drawRect (SkDrawBase.cpp:230)
SkBitmapDevice::drawRect (SkBitmapDevice.cpp:354)
SkBitmapDevice::drawImageRect (SkBitmapDevice.cpp:530)
SkCanvas::onDrawImageRect2 (SkCanvas.cpp:2328)
viz::SoftwareRenderer::DrawTileQuad (software_renderer.cc:524)
viz::SoftwareRenderer::DoDrawQuad (software_renderer.cc:360)
viz::DirectRenderer::DrawRenderPass (direct_renderer.cc:838)
viz::DirectRenderer::DrawFrame (direct_renderer.cc:435)
viz::Display::DrawAndSwap (display.cc:1034)
viz::DisplayScheduler::DrawAndSwap (display_scheduler.cc:269)

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

claude analyze below:

Root cause (hypothesis)

gather_8888 uses the AVX2 vpgatherdd instruction to batch-load 8 pixels at once from a source tile bitmap during compositing. This appears to be an out-of-bounds read near the edge of a scaled/clipped source image — a known recurring class of bug in Skia's SIMD raster pipeline (e.g. Mozilla bug [1568858](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1568858), [CVE-2021-29968](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1712047)), which historically manifests in the CPU/software-compositing path. When the source buffer's last valid bytes happen to sit at a page boundary, the over-read crosses into unmapped memory and triggers the access violation.

Why --disable-gpu doesn't help

--disable-gpu forces Chromium into viz::SoftwareRenderer, which performs compositing via Skia's CPU raster pipeline — including the AVX2 hsw::lowp code path that's crashing. Disabling the GPU therefore increases exposure to this bug rather than avoiding it.

Reproduction status

Not yet isolated to a specific page/content pattern; happens under normal software-compositing usage after the 22.3.6 → 34.5.8 upgrade. Working on narrowing down a minimal repro (image size/DPI scaling/tile boundary conditions).

Workaround

Launching with --disable-skia-runtime-opts (forces Skia to fall back to the SSE2 implementation, avoiding the AVX2 vpgatherdd path entirely) appears to be a viable mitigation, pending validation.

Ask
Is this a known/tracked issue in Skia's raster pipeline (gather_8888 bounds handling)?
Has this been fixed in any Chromium/Skia version between M108 (Electron 22.3.6) and M132+ (Electron 34.5.8), or in a later version we could reference for a fix/backport?
Any guidance on a minimal repro pattern that reliably triggers this gather stage would be appreciated.

### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.4.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.6 (25G72) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No. This is specific to Electron's ASAR filesystem integration. ### Expected Behavior After a temporary copy of a packed ASAR entry is removed while Electron remains running, a later `fs.createReadStream()` call for that ASAR entry should recreate the temporary copy or otherwise read the packed bytes successfully. ### Actual Behavior The first `fs.createReadStream()` succeeds. If its extracted temporary file is then deleted while Electron remains running, every later `fs.createReadStream()` for the same ASAR entry fails with `ENOENT` for the deleted temporary pathname. A buffered `fs.readFileSync()` of the same packed entry continues to succeed. Example output from the testcase: ```text Extracted copy: /var/folders/.../T/.com.github.Electron.ul88vz Deleted the extracted copy while Electron remains running. readFileSync after deletion: "electron-asar-stale-cache-repro-7e8fa4f9\n" REPRODUCED: ENOENT opening cached path /var/folders/.../T/.com.github.Electron.ul88vz ``` ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/0xdevalias/b28e27ea290913bbe4510eeaad7edaf3 Run with: ```sh git clone https://gist.github.com/b28e27ea290913bbe4510eeaad7edaf3.git cd b28e27ea290913bbe4510eeaad7edaf3 npm install npm start ``` ### Additional Information This was first encountered in openai/codex#37551, where a long-running Electron process could no longer open Codex windows after its extracted `.com.openai.codex.*` ASAR files disappeared. The original packed entries remained readable, and recreating the expected temporary files restored the running application. The validated diagnosis and workaround are documented in openai/codex#37551 (especially [this investigation comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37551#issuecomment-5278987637) and [the upstream-context follow-up](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37551#issuecomment-5279309264)). - openai/codex#37551 This report is specifically about recovery from a missing cached extraction file, rather than whether temporary files should be cleaned up at process exit. Related prior reports: - #30911 - reports the same temporary-file lifetime problem for an ASAR-backed tray icon after the temp directory is cleared. It was closed for inactivity rather than by a generic cache fix. - #22500 - notes that the OS may clean files from the temporary directory while the application is alive. - #29293 - made the ASAR archive cache process-wide. That fixed #29292, but also makes the archive's extracted-path cache long-lived. - #52424 - recently avoided `CopyFileOut()` for one packed-ICO call site, but did not change generic missing-file recovery.
In-depth investigation

`Archive::CopyFileOut()` retains extracted files in `external_files_`. Its cache-hit branch returns the stored pathname without checking whether it still exists: - https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/common/asar/archive.cc#L354-L390 Electron's Node filesystem wrapper calls `archive.copyFileOut()` from its `fs.open()` override. `fs.createReadStream()` reaches that wrapper, so a later stream open receives the stale pathname and the underlying OS open fails with `ENOENT`: - https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/node/asar-fs-wrapper.ts#L179-L237 - https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/node/asar-fs-wrapper.ts#L1218-L1229 The standalone testcase uses only the public `fs` behavior to trigger the failure. It locates the first extracted copy by its unique contents, deletes it, confirms `readFileSync()` can still read the original packed bytes, and then observes `createReadStream()` failing against the same deleted pathname. Electron's own ASAR URL loader already avoids extraction for packed entries and streams from a duplicate of the archive's retained file handle. PR #52283 similarly made retained-handle reads robust when an updater atomically replaces `app.asar`. Neither path repairs a missing `CopyFileOut()` cache entry. A minimal fix could check the cached path under `external_files_lock_`, evict the entry when it no longer exists, and extract it again. A fully race-resistant solution may also need retry/invalidation if the file disappears between an existence check and the consumer's subsequent `open()`.

nodes.title: Expose destructive buttons in macOS message boxes
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description Electron applications cannot currently identify a `dialog.showMessageBox()` button as destructive on macOS. AppKit provides [`NSButton.hasDestructiveAction`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsbutton/hasdestructiveaction) for this purpose. Apple recommends setting it for actions that can irretrievably discard user data, allowing the system to apply an appropriate appearance and safeguards against accidental presses. This came up in [microsoft/vscode#325273](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325273), where a native three-button `Save` / `Don't Save` / `Cancel` prompt could initially give `Don't Save` keyboard focus when macOS Keyboard Navigation was enabled. Space would then discard unsaved work. VS Code has since mitigated that immediate problem by changing its button ordering, but Electron still cannot express the underlying semantic: “this button performs a destructive action.” Application code must instead rely on button order, labels, or a custom non-native dialog. ### Proposed Solution Add an optional macOS-only destructive button index to `MessageBoxOptions`, analogous to `defaultId` and `cancelId`: ```js dialog.showMessageBox(window, { buttons: ['Save', "Don't Save", 'Cancel'], defaultId: 0, destructiveId: 1, cancelId: 2, message: 'Do you want to save your changes?' }) ``` On macOS, Electron would set `hasDestructiveAction = YES` on the corresponding `NSButton` in the native `NSAlert`. Existing button indices, response values, default-button behavior, and cancel behavior would remain unchanged. Other platforms could ignore the macOS-only option. The main question I would like maintainer feedback on is whether this is an appropriate Electron API and whether a singular `destructiveId` is the right minimal shape. ### Alternatives Considered - Applications can reorder their buttons to influence which button receives initial keyboard focus. This can mitigate a particular accidental-input path, as VS Code has done, but it does not identify the action as destructive or allow AppKit to apply its destructive-action behavior. - Applications can use custom HTML dialogs. That provides complete control but gives up the native dialog and its platform behavior. - Electron could infer destructive actions from labels such as `Delete` or `Don't Save`. That would be unreliable, difficult to localize, and surprising compared with an explicit option. ### Additional Information I created an AI-assisted prototype to test the API shape and observable AppKit behavior before proposing a production PR: - [Prototype branch](https://github.com/joshka/electron/tree/joshka/destructive-message-box) - [Electron implementation commit](https://github.com/joshka/electron/commit/d175f19e821f) - [Manual Electron and native AppKit probes](https://github.com/joshka/electron/commit/323feb78f018) The implementation commit passes the option through Electron's existing message-box conversion path, applies `hasDestructiveAction` in the macOS `NSAlert` implementation, documents the option, and adds automated coverage. The second commit deliberately keeps the manual probes separate. In testing on macOS Sequoia 15.7.7 with Keyboard Navigation enabled, setting `hasDestructiveAction` on `Don't Save` changed the initial keyboard focus from `Don't Save` to `Cancel` for the button insertion order involved in the VS Code report. That observation motivates the proposal, but AppKit behavior can vary by macOS version and context; Electron should expose the semantic rather than promise a particular focus outcome. I am opening this issue for buy-in on the API and behavior before turning the prototype into a production contribution. The implementation itself is inexpensive to produce; agreement on the public API and expected cross-version semantics is the important part.

```js
dialog.showMessageBox(window, {
  buttons: ['Save', "Don't Save", 'Cancel'],
  defaultId: 0,
  destructiveId: 1,
  cancelId: 2,
  message: 'Do you want to save your changes?'
})
```

On macOS, Electron would set `hasDestructiveAction = YES` on the corresponding `NSButton` in the native `NSAlert`. Existing button indices, response values, default-button behavior, and cancel behavior would remain unchanged. Other platforms could ignore the macOS-only option.

The main question I would like maintainer feedback on is whether this is an appropriate Electron API and whether a singular `destructiveId` is the right minimal shape.

### Alternatives Considered

- Applications can reorder their buttons to influence which button receives initial keyboard focus. This can mitigate a particular accidental-input path, as VS Code has done, but it does not identify the action as destructive or allow AppKit to apply its destructive-action behavior.
- Applications can use custom HTML dialogs. That provides complete control but gives up the native dialog and its platform behavior.
- Electron could infer destructive actions from labels such as `Delete` or `Don't Save`. That would be unreliable, difficult to localize, and surprising compared with an explicit option.

### Additional Information

I created an AI-assisted prototype to test the API shape and observable AppKit behavior before proposing a production PR:

- [Prototype branch](https://github.com/joshka/electron/tree/joshka/destructive-message-box)
- [Electron implementation commit](https://github.com/joshka/electron/commit/d175f19e821f)
- [Manual Electron and native AppKit probes](https://github.com/joshka/electron/commit/323feb78f018)

The implementation commit passes the option through Electron's existing message-box conversion path, applies `hasDestructiveAction` in the macOS `NSAlert` implementation, documents the option, and adds automated coverage. The second commit deliberately keeps the manual probes separate.

In testing on macOS Sequoia 15.7.7 with Keyboard Navigation enabled, setting `hasDestructiveAction` on `Don't Save` changed the initial keyboard focus from `Don't Save` to `Cancel` for the button insertion order involved in the VS Code report. That observation motivates the proposal, but AppKit behavior can vary by macOS version and context; Electron should expose the semantic rather than promise a particular focus outcome.

I am opening this issue for buy-in on the API and behavior before turning the prototype into a production contribution. The implementation itself is inexpensive to produce; agreement on the public API and expected cross-version semantics is the important part.

### Expected Behavior

## Environment

* **Electron:** 35.0.0
* **Electron Forge:** 7.4.0
* **Platform:** macOS

## Background

We are building a reusable Electron framework that is used to generate customer applications.

During a security assessment, we noticed that the generated macOS `Info.plist` contains the following configuration:

```xml
<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
    <key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
```

We did not explicitly configure this setting in our application.

We traced it back to Electron's macOS `Info.plist` template:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v30.0.0/shell/browser/resources/mac/Info.plist

Since `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true` disables ATS restrictions for applicable network requests, this setting was flagged during our security assessment.

## Testing

We tested the behavior with Electron 35.0.0 using both configurations.

### Test 1 — `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: true`

Request:

```text
http://httpbin.org/get
```

### Test 2 — `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: false`

Request:

```text
http://httpbin.org/get
```

We tested the request using `net.fetch()`.

In both cases, the HTTP request showed the same behavior. Setting `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` to `false` did not appear to prevent the HTTP request.

Because of this, we are unclear about which Electron networking APIs or request paths are actually affected by macOS App Transport Security (ATS).

## Current Workaround

We are currently overriding Electron's default configuration through our packaging configuration:

```javascript
extendInfo: {
    NSAppTransportSecurity: {
        NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: false,
    },
},
```

So far, we have not observed any functional issues with this configuration.

## Questions

We would appreciate clarification on the following:

1. Why does Electron set `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true` by default in the macOS `Info.plist`?

2. Is this setting required for any specific Electron functionality?

3. Which Electron networking APIs are actually affected by macOS ATS?
   For example:

   * `net.fetch()`
   * `net.request()`
   * Chromium renderer requests (`fetch`, XHR, etc.)
   * `<webview>` or navigation requests
   * any other Electron networking paths

4. Is it expected that `net.fetch()` can access an HTTP endpoint even when `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=false`?

5. Is overriding `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` to `false` fully supported and safe for Electron applications that do not require arbitrary HTTP access?

6. Are there any known Electron features or networking scenarios that could stop working when this value is changed to `false`?

Our goal is to keep the more restrictive ATS configuration for security compliance while ensuring that we do not unintentionally break any Electron functionality.

```xml
<dict>
    <key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
```

even when the application does not explicitly configure this property.

Because of this, it is unclear whether macOS ATS restrictions apply to `net.fetch()` and which Electron networking APIs are actually affected by this configuration.

nodes.title: Windows: dns.getServers() returns 127.0.0.1 and dns.resolveSrv() fails with ECONNREFUSED
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.7.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 PRO 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron's embedded Node.js DNS resolver should use the DNS servers configured in the Windows network stack. When the native Windows resolver can resolve a public SRV record, dns.getServers() should expose the effective non-loopback DNS server(s), and dns.promises.resolveSrv() should return the SRV records.

### Actual Behavior

On an affected Windows x64 machine, Electron 42.7.0 (Node.js 24.18.0, c-ares 1.34.6) returns only [ '127.0.0.1' ] from dns.getServers(), even though Windows has a working non-loopback DNS server and nothing is listening on 127.0.0.1:53.

dns.promises.resolveSrv() then fails with:

~~~text
Error: querySrv ECONNREFUSED _incallapp_sip._tcp.domain.com
~~~

The native Windows resolver resolves the same public SRV record successfully. This prevents a production Electron application from discovering its service endpoint and blocks login.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

> Privacy note: the DNS query name and SRV target shown in this report have been anonymized using `domain.com`.

### Minimal main-process reproduction

~~~js
const { app } = require('electron');
const dns = require('node:dns');

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  console.log('versions:', process.versions);
  console.log('servers:', dns.getServers());

  try {
    const records = await dns.promises.resolveSrv(
      '_incallapp_sip._tcp.domain.com'
    );
    console.log('records:', records);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
  } finally {
    app.quit();
  }
});
~~~

### Steps

1. Install Electron 42.7.0 in a minimal application with the snippet above as main.js.
2. On a Windows machine showing the affected DNS configuration, run the native query below.
3. Run the application with npx electron . and compare the results.

On the affected machine, the native resolver succeeds:

~~~powershell
Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _incallapp_sip._tcp.domain.com
~~~

It returns target service.domain.com on port 5022. Running the Electron snippet on the same machine prints [ '127.0.0.1' ] and throws ECONNREFUSED. The system-installed Node.js is not involved; the failure occurs in Electron's main process using its embedded runtime.

The condition is machine-dependent, but it matches multiple independent Windows reports in the upstream Node.js issue.

### Upstream root cause and fix

This matches nodejs/node#62347:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62347

The bug is in the Windows c-ares system configuration code. An empty Registry wide string is checked using size == 1 instead of size == sizeof(WCHAR), which can cause the Windows DNS configuration to be discarded and c-ares to fall back to loopback.

The fix was merged in nodejs/node#64110:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/64110

It is included in Node.js 24.19.0:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.19.0/doc/changelogs/CHANGELOG_V24.md#2026-08-03-version-24190-krypton-lts-aduh95

Electron 42.9.0 still embeds Node.js 24.18.1, whose c-ares source retains the faulty check:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.9.0/DEPS#L3-L8

### Why this needs tracking in Electron

Electron applications cannot replace the embedded Node.js runtime with the system-installed Node.js. Therefore, even though the upstream defect is fixed, applications on supported Electron releases remain affected until Electron updates its embedded Node.js or backports the c-ares patch.

The direct workaround is to call dns.setServers() with hard-coded public resolvers. That is not generally safe for production applications because it can bypass enterprise DNS policy, VPN/split-DNS configuration, and private zones.

### Suggested resolution

Please update the embedded Node.js runtime to 24.19.0 in the supported Electron release lines, or backport the small c-ares fix from nodejs/node#64110 until the dependency bump is available.

I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior For an offscreen-rendered page, a reversed wheel packet should be retargeted to the scrollable element under the pointer after the preceding direction was unconsumed at a scroll boundary. ### Actual Behavior After an unconsumed wheel packet at the top boundary, reversing the direction does not scroll the nested container under the pointer. The nested container remains at its top boundary. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/eric8810/3c54f310f196ea987a7ebcbf42ce2bd5 ### Additional Information The issue reproduces with ordinary `offscreen: true`; shared-texture output is not required. A proposed fix and regression spec are in #52776.
In-depth investigation

`OffScreenRenderWidgetHostView::SendMouseWheelEvent()` lets `MouseWheelPhaseHandler` update a mutable copy of the event but forwards the original event. The view also does not feed gesture acknowledgements back into the phase handler. Forwarding the adjusted event and handling `GestureEventAck()` allows the reversed packet to begin a new sequence at the point under the pointer.

nodes.title: Windows: dialog.showMessageBox auto-closes and returns a fabricated button index (420) for a button that was never created
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.3.0 (Also verified on 42.8.1 and 36.9.1)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 26200.8973, Windows 10 

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None. The affected code is unchanged in v20.3.12, v25.9.8, v30.5.1, v36.9.1 and v43.3.0, so this appears to have been present since custom buttons were introduced.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a message box is closed by a button id that Electron did not create, the
returned `response` should not be a valid-looking index into `buttons`. Returning
`cancelId` (the existing fallback for unknown ids below `kIDStart`) would be
consistent and safe.

### Actual Behavior

> **Scope, up front:** the dialog is closed by comctl32 before
> `TaskDialogIndirect` returns, so Electron cannot prevent the dismissal and this
> issue does not ask it to. The bug being reported is the **`response` value**:
> Electron fabricates a valid-looking button index from an id it never created,
> which is what makes the failure silent and undiagnosable in application code.

`showMessageBox` / `showMessageBoxSync` return `response: 420` for a message box
that has two buttons. Application code that branches on `response === 0` takes the
"no" path with no indication that anything unusual happened, and nothing is logged.

The cause is an unbounded range check in
[`shell/browser/ui/message_box_win.cc`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.3.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_win.cc#L259):

```cpp
int id = 0;
BOOL verification_flag_checked = FALSE;
TaskDialogIndirect(&config, &id, nullptr, &verification_flag_checked);

int button_id;
if (id_map.contains(id))  // common button.
  button_id = id_map[id];
else if (id >= kIDStart)  // custom button.
  button_id = id - kIDStart;      // <-- no upper bound
else
  button_id = cancel_id;
```

Any `id >= kIDStart` (100) is treated as a custom button, so an id of 520 becomes
`response: 420` even when only two buttons were configured. The check never
compares against `dialog_buttons.size()`.

### Suggested fix

```cpp
else if (id >= kIDStart && id - kIDStart < static_cast<int>(buttons.size()))
  button_id = id - kIDStart;
else
  button_id = cancel_id;
```


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/itsjithinv/16e9fde9bb666a4d0e25244a5db52ca3

### Additional Information

### Why an id we never created arrives at all

`0x0466` is `TDM_CLICK_BUTTON` for a TaskDialog and `CDM_GETFOLDERPATH` for a
common file dialog — the same message number, and both dialog types use window
class `#32770`. Software that reads the current folder out of file dialogs (file
dialog enhancers, DLP and endpoint agents) enumerates `#32770` windows and sends
`0x0466` with `wParam` = buffer size and `lParam` = buffer pointer. On a file
dialog that is a legitimate query and the dialog stays open. On an Electron
message box, comctl32 interprets `wParam` as a button id and ends the dialog.

`wParam` is typically `0x208` = 520 = `MAX_PATH` in bytes, which is why the
fabricated index is consistently 420.

### Scope of the request

comctl32 closes the dialog before `TaskDialogIndirect` returns, so Electron cannot
prevent the dismissal — that part is not what this issue asks for. The request is
only that Electron not fabricate a plausible button index from an id it never
created. With the fix, an app receives `cancelId` and behaves as though the user
cancelled, instead of silently falling through every branch.

### Real-world impact

We traced this in a production Electron app where a close-confirmation dialog
appeared and vanished within ~250 ms for 100+ users. Because `response` was 420
rather than any configured id, the app neither quit nor logged anything, and the
issue was undiagnosable from telemetry for a long time. Spy++ captures show no
`WM_COMMAND`, no `WM_CLOSE`, no keyboard or mouse input on the dialog — the last
message before teardown is `0x0466 wParam:00000208`.

Verified in a minimal app (below) with no application code involved: every native
message box variant — with parent, without parent, one/two/three buttons, sync and
async — returns 420, while `showOpenDialog` on the same machine is unaffected.

### Minimal reproduction

`main.js`:

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow, dialog } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  // A window is only needed to keep the app alive.
  new BrowserWindow({ show: true, width: 400, height: 200 });

  const { response } = await dialog.showMessageBox({
    type: 'question',
    buttons: ['Quit', 'Cancel'],   // valid responses are 0 and 1
    cancelId: 1,
    message: 'Are you sure you want to quit?'
  });

  console.log('response:', response);   // 420
});
```

Reproduce the foreign message deterministically — run this in 64-bit PowerShell
while the message box is on screen, no third-party software required:

```powershell
Add-Type -Namespace R -Name W -MemberDefinition @'
  [DllImport("user32.dll")]
  public static extern IntPtr FindWindowExW(IntPtr p, IntPtr c, string cls, string title);
  [DllImport("user32.dll")]
  public static extern IntPtr SendMessageW(IntPtr h, uint m, IntPtr w, IntPtr l);
'@

# First top-level #32770 window; narrow by title if other dialogs are open.
$h = [R.W]::FindWindowExW([IntPtr]::Zero, [IntPtr]::Zero, '#32770', $null)
$buf = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::AllocHGlobal(520)
[void][R.W]::SendMessageW($h, 0x0466, [IntPtr]520, $buf)   # wParam 520 = MAX_PATH bytes
[System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::FreeHGlobal($buf)
```

The dialog closes and the app prints `response: 420`.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.3.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 (arm64 / Apple Silicon) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — have not found a version where this works via a custom picker. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When `session.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` is used with `useSystemPicker: false` (i.e. the app supplies its own picker UI and resolves the callback with a `desktopCapturer` source plus `audio: 'loopback'` or `audio: 'loopbackWithMute'`), the resulting audio `MediaStreamTrack` should actually capture system audio, the same way it does when `useSystemPicker: true` is used instead. ### Actual Behavior The audio track is created (`kind: "audio"`, `label: "System audio"`), so the API call itself succeeds, but the track's `readyState` is `"ended"` from the very first observation, and no audio data is ever captured — an `AnalyserNode` attached to the track reports `peakAmplitude: 0` at every sample, forever. The video track from the same `getDisplayMedia()` call works fine (`readyState: "live"`, frames render normally) — only the audio side fails. Swapping the same request handler to `useSystemPicker: true` (letting Electron/macOS own the whole picker UI) makes system-audio capture work correctly and also correctly triggers the macOS "would like to record system audio" TCC permission prompt. With `useSystemPicker: false`, that TCC prompt never appears at all — which is consistent with the underlying native audio-capture session never actually starting, even though the JS-level API returns a track as if it had. This makes `audio: 'loopback'`/`'loopbackWithMute'` unusable for any app that wants to keep its own custom screen-share picker UI while also offering a "share system audio" option — the only way to get working system audio is to hand the entire picker over to `useSystemPicker: true`, which replaces the app's own UI. Reproduces identically on an ad-hoc `electron .` run and on a `Developer ID`-signed, hardened-runtime, notarization-skipped, `/Applications`-installed packaged build — so this isn't a code-signing or Gatekeeper/TCC-staleness issue. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/anildigital/9a195654a687524fb544db62894466fe ### Additional Information Steps to reproduce with the gist: 1. `npm install` in the gist's directory, then `npm start` (or `electron .`). 2. The renderer calls `getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true })`. 3. Watch the on-screen log: the audio track appears with `readyState=ended` immediately, and the peak-amplitude readout stays at `0.0000` indefinitely, while the video track stays `live`. 4. For comparison, change `useSystemPicker: false` to `useSystemPicker: true` in `main.js` and repeat — the native macOS picker appears, the TCC "record your system audio" prompt fires, and after granting it, real audio is captured (non-zero peak amplitude).
In-depth investigation

We believe the root cause is that macOS's system-audio capture (the ScreenCaptureKit-backed Core Audio Tap, gated behind the separate "System Audio Recording Only" TCC permission introduced in newer macOS versions) is only ever started by Electron when Electron's own native picker (`useSystemPicker: true`) drives the capture end-to-end. When an app supplies its own `desktopCapturer`-selected source through a custom picker instead, the `'loopback'`/`'loopbackWithMute'` audio request appears to be accepted and a track handle is handed back, but the corresponding native capture session is never actually wired up — no TCC prompt is ever shown for the app through this path, and `getUserMedia`/`getDisplayMedia` never delivers audio samples. We were unable to find any workaround from the app side (no combination of Chromium command-line switches changed the result), and confirmed the failure is independent of code signing, notarization, and running from `/Applications` vs. an ad-hoc build directory.
